title: Palm Drive
blurb: The palm-lined avenue from El Camino Real to the Oval, and most visitors' first view of campus.

title: The Oval
blurb: The great lawn at the top of Palm Drive, framing the view of the Main Quad and Memorial Church.

title: Main Quad
blurb: The original heart of campus, opened in 1891: sandstone buildings and arcades with red tile roofs, laid out with Frederick Law Olmsted.

title: Memorial Church
blurb: Built by Jane Stanford in memory of her husband Leland and dedicated in 1903. Its mosaic facade faces the inner Quad.

title: Hoover Tower
blurb: The 285-foot tower finished in 1941 for Stanford's 50th anniversary, home to part of the Hoover Institution Library & Archives.

title: Green Library
blurb: Cecil H. Green Library, Stanford's main humanities and social sciences library. The Bing Wing is the original 1919 library.

title: White Plaza
blurb: The student crossroads between Tresidder, Old Union and the Bookstore, with club tables and the Claw fountain.

title: Tresidder Union
blurb: The student union: food, meeting rooms and services just off White Plaza.

title: Old Union
blurb: Stanford's original student union, now home to student life offices and community centers.

title: Cantor Arts Center
blurb: Stanford's art museum, opened in 1894 as the Leland Stanford Junior Museum.

title: Rodin Sculpture Garden
blurb: An outdoor garden of bronzes by Auguste Rodin beside the Cantor, including The Gates of Hell.

title: Anderson Collection
blurb: A museum of modern and contemporary American art next to the Cantor.

title: Bing Concert Hall
blurb: The concert hall opened in 2013, built around a vineyard-style auditorium.

title: Frost Amphitheater
blurb: An open-air concert bowl in the trees, dedicated in 1937.

title: Stanford Stadium
blurb: Home of Stanford football, rebuilt in 2006 inside the bowl of the original 1921 stadium.

title: Maples Pavilion
blurb: Home of Stanford basketball and volleyball since 1969.

title: Sunken Diamond
blurb: Klein Field at Sunken Diamond, Stanford's baseball park.

title: Science & Engineering Quad
blurb: The SEQ, ringed by Huang, Y2E2, Spilker and the Shriram Center.

title: Gates Computer Science
blurb: Home of the Computer Science department since 1996.

title: Stanford Law School
blurb: The Law School's Crown Quadrangle, on the east side of the Main Quad.

title: Lake Lagunita
blurb: A seasonal lake: it fills in wet winters and dries to meadow the rest of the year.

title: Roble Hall
blurb: Opened in 1918 as a women's residence, now a co-ed dorm near Lake Lag.

title: Florence Moore Hall
blurb: FloMo: seven student houses (Alondra, Cardenal, Faisan, Gavilan, Loro, Mirlo and Paloma) with their own dining hall.

title: Lagunita Court
blurb: Houses around a courtyard near the lake, including Adelfa, Eucalipto, Granada, Naranja, Meier, Norcliffe and Ujamaa.

title: Governor's Corner
blurb: Suites and houses at the west edge of campus, including Robinson, Yost, Potter and Murray.

title: The Row
blurb: Mayfield Avenue and its neighbours, lined with student houses, co-ops and Greek houses.

title: Wilbur Hall
blurb: Eight houses, mostly for first-year students: Arroyo, Cedro, Junipero, Okada, Otero, Rinconada, Soto and Trancos.

title: Stern Hall
blurb: Six houses: Burbank, Donner, Larkin, Sally Ride, Twain and Casa Zapata.

title: Branner Hall
blurb: A large residence next to Toyon and Crothers.

title: Gerhard Casper Quad
blurb: Kimball, Lantana, Castaño and Ng houses around a shared dining commons.

title: Escondido Village
blurb: Graduate housing east of campus, from low-rise apartments to the EVGR towers opened in 2020.

title: Stanford Hospital
blurb: The medical center on the north edge of campus; the new hospital opened in 2019.
